fields.mechanism: Cementite in the pearlite phase acts as a cathode that promotes dissolution of surrounding ferrite, accelerating localized corrosion at inclusion sites.
fields.intervention: Apply targeted induction heat treatment to the external surface of sleeve joints through small access ports to spheroidize or dissolve the cementite network within the pearlite fraction, eliminating the continuous cathodic phase without excavating or relining the 60-kilometer network.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of the micro-galvanic couple between cementite and ferrite halts the electrochemical acceleration of pitting at aluminum inclusions and other crevice sites, arresting chloride-induced pit propagation at the joints.
fields.falsification_test: Extract a core sample from a treated sleeve joint, measure the pearlite fraction and cementite morphology via metallography, and perform potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5% NaCl solution; if the treated steel exhibits a pitting potential equal to or lower than untreated baseline steel, the mechanism is falsified.
fields.mechanism_source_span: In the large pearlite fraction region, cementite in the pearlite acted as a cathode to promote dissolution of surrounding ferrite.

fields.falsification_test: Extract coupon samples from heat-treated sleeve joint zones and perform potentiodynamic polarization testing in simulated chloride-contaminated groundwater; if pitting potential does not shift anodically relative to untreated baseline steel, the intervention fails.

fields.mechanism: Cementite in pearlite acts as a cathode to promote dissolution of surrounding ferrite, accelerating localized corrosion.
fields.intervention: Apply localized induction heating at insulating sleeve joints to raise the steel surface temperature above 80°C, spheroidizing the cementite lamellae within the pearlite phase into discrete globular particles, thereby eliminating the continuous cathodic network that drives accelerated anodic dissolution of ferrite under chloride attack without excavation.
fields.expected_effect: Disruption of the continuous cementite cathode network reduces the galvanic driving force for ferrite dissolution, arresting the acceleration of external pitting at sleeve joints and extending remaining service life beyond the original 40-year design target.
fields.falsification_test: Extract a core sample from a sleeve joint after localized induction treatment, perform metallographic analysis to confirm cementite spheroidization, and conduct potentiodynamic polarization testing in simulated road-salt groundwater to measure whether the pitting potential shifts positively by at least 150 mV compared to untreated baseline samples.

fields.mechanism: Cementite in the pearlite phase acts as a cathode to promote electrochemical dissolution of surrounding ferrite, accelerating localized corrosion at microstructural inhomogeneities.
fields.intervention: Inject a thermally conductive, electrically insulating two-part epoxy resin into the annular space at sleeve joints through small drill ports; the district heating fluid provides the thermal domain (elevated temperature accelerates resin curing and lowers viscosity for capillary penetration) while the cured resin provides the electrical domain (high dielectric strength breaks the galvanic circuit between cementite cathodes and ferrite anodes), directly suppressing the cementite-cathode/ferrite-anode mechanism without excavation.
fields.expected_effect: The electrically insulating barrier eliminates ionic current flow between the cathodic cementite and anodic ferrite phases, halting chloride-induced pitting propagation at sleeve joints and extending service life beyond the 40-year design target without full network relining.
fields.falsification_test: Extract core samples from injected sleeve joints after 12 months of operation, perform scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy to map cementite-ferrite interfaces, and measure localized galvanic current density using micro-reference electrodes; if active dissolution of ferrite adjacent to cementite is still detected, the intervention has failed.

fields.mechanism: Crevice corrosion occurs in the vicinity around aluminum inclusions, and cementite in pearlite acts as a cathode to promote dissolution of surrounding ferrite, accelerating localized corrosion.
fields.intervention: Inject a targeted alkaline inhibitor slurry through existing vent or drain ports into the annular space at insulating sleeve joints to chemically passivate the aluminum inclusions and suppress the cathodic activity of cementite on the external steel surface without excavation.
fields.expected_effect: The injected inhibitor neutralizes the crevice environment around aluminum inclusions and blocks the galvanic coupling between cementite and ferrite, arresting chloride-induced pitting propagation at sleeve joints and extending remaining service life beyond the 40-year design target.
fields.falsification_test: Extract localized groundwater samples from the annular space at treated sleeve joints after 6 months; if dissolved iron concentration remains above 0.5 mg/L or electrochemical noise measurements indicate active pit propagation, the intervention has failed.
